Subject: Finova decision criteria  latency / cost / deployment / SLA clarification

Hi Eric / Priya 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and action items from our discovery:

Key decision criteria you called out:
- Latency: target P95 <= 200ms for single-turn text-generation at pilot shape (up to ~250 tokens).
- Cost: target competitive unit economics for pilot  internal goal expressed as <$0.06 per 1k tokens (pilot).
- Deployment: preference for Dedicated (reserved capacity) but open to Private deployment if procurement/security requires VPC / on-prem.
- SLA: business-critical availability with a requested 99.9% uptime and defined incident response (on-call + 4-hour initial response).

Stakeholder mapping we discussed:
- Economic buyer: Amit Rao (CFO)  priority on predictable monthly spend and reserved capacity pricing.
- Security / Legal: Priya Sen (Head of Legal / Procurement) and procurement team.
- Technical / Infra: Eric Lawson (Lead ML/Infra) and additional infra engineers for the technical deep-dive.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Ill share a short doc outlining deployment options (Dedicated vs Private), typical latency profiles, and SLA tiers  Rafael will add expected performance numbers for the pilot shape. (Attached: Redwood-deployment-options.pdf)
2) Rafael / Nikhil to run a short technical deep-dive with Eric + infra team next week to validate p95 numbers and discuss traffic shaping / KV caching.
3) Priya / Procurement: please share the security questionnaire / required docs; well prioritize SOC 2 + KMS/HSM details.
4) Marissa will capture a mutual action plan with timelines and a recommended pricing band for pilot.

If I missed anything or priorities shifted, let me know. Otherwise Rafael / Nikhil  can you propose 2x slots next week for the tech call?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria  latency / cost / deployment / SLA clarification

Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side after chatting with Amit and the infra team:

Latency / Performance
- P95 <= 200ms is our target for the customer-facing flows (single-turn, ~200200300 token outputs). We recognize that multi-turn/contextual flows may have higher latency; we need guidance on how Redwood maintains consistent P95 as context length grows.

Cost
- Amit asked us to treat cost conservatively for the initial SOW: pilot target of <$0.05 per 1k tokens (including any caching assumptions). Well evaluate based on measured token counts during pilot.

Deployment / SLA
- Preference is Dedicated for pilot (reserved capacity) to get predictable throughput; however, Security is evaluating Private VPC if we need on-prem key management.
- SLA: 99.9% is the ask; for procurement we’ll need specifics on credits, MTTR, and escalation paths.

Procurement timeline
- Procurement (Priya + team) estimates 68 weeks to complete PO & contract review once we have the security artifacts and the SOW.

Action items for Redwood
- Share the deployment options doc (received).
- Can you include an expected P95 profile for the pilot model (1k QPS burst, steady-state 300 qps) and a breakdown of what changes for Private vs Dedicated?
- Please share SOC 2 attestation + KMS/HSM details for the security review.

Ill coordinate schedules for the technical deep-dive  available Tue/Wed next week (PST).

Eric
Eric Lawson
Lead, ML Infrastructure | Finova
eric.lawson@finova.com

Eric 

Appreciate the quick clarifications. A few notes and attachments to make the procurement/security review easier:

1) Deployment & performance notes (high level)  see attached Redwood-deployment-options.pdf
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, lower variance on P95; recommended for pilot to match your predictability requirements. We’ve included sample P95 numbers for a 256-token generation shape at 300 qps and an approach for autoscaling headrooms.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): gives you full network isolation and option for customer-managed KMS/HSM; operational overhead is higher and SLA adjustments are typically required depending on connectivity.

2) Performance profile (pilot assumptions)  Rafael and engineering note:
- Pilot model (256 tokens): expected P95 ~ 120180ms on Dedicated (NVIDIA H100-like class), with continuous batching and KV caching enabled.
- P95 increases with longer contexts; caching + compilation choices can keep user-facing P95 within target for most flows.

3) Cost assumptions & options  high-level
- Typical pilot pricing bands (reserved capacity): expected to meet target in the vicinity of $0.040.06 per 1k tokens depending on steady-state utilization and caching hit rate. We’ll model this more precisely after the tech call (Rafael).

4) SLA / support options
- We offer 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated with defined crediting matrix, 4-hour initial incident response for P1, and named escalation contacts for enterprise plans. We’ll include the exact SLA language in the SOW.

Attachments included: Redwood-deployment-options.pdf, Finova-security-questions.xlsx (prefilled template with SOC 2 + KMS notes). Rafael  can you add the detailed P95 numbers and one-slide appendix on cache + batching assumptions before EOD?

Next steps:
- Rafael to propose 2x slots for the technical deep-dive (I can host a calendar invite).
- Priya / Procurement: if you can share the procurement checklist or any contract templates we should review, we’ll start prep work.

Thanks,

Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Economic buyer (Amit Rao) will review the pricing band and reserve final sign-off for budget allocation.

DocuSign / Contract:

For scheduling: procurement will join the technical deep-dive if there are questions about network isolation or KMS.
